pdcchAggRarespHo.description:
PDCCH aggregation for contention free Random Access response message and minimum PDCCH aggregation for HARQ retransmissions of a non-contention based Random Access Procedure initial transmission defines how many effective CCEs (actual CCEs + CCE power boost) are used for one PDCCH:
Value of 4 = 4 CCEs + 0 dB power boost
Value of 8 = 8 CCEs + 0 dB power boost
Value of 12 = 8 CCEs + 1.8 dB power boost
Value of 16 = 8 CCEs + 3 dB power boost
pdcchAggRarespHo.fullName: PDCCH aggregation for contention free random access response message
pdcchAggRarespHo.notes:
Related functions: PHY/MAC Configuration (Downlink) Related parameters: LNCEL - cellTechnology
LNCEL_FDD - dlChBw
LNCEL_FDD - maxNrSymPdcch
LNCEL_TDD - chBw Conditions in (1.x) are valid if the cellTechnology of the LNCEL instance is configured to 'FDD' or 'TDD':
(1.1) pdcchAggRarespHo must be configured.

Conditions in (2.x) are valid in addition to (1.x) if the cellTechnology is configured to 'FDD':
(2.1) pdcchAggRarespHo must be configured to '4' in all of the following cases:
- dlChBw set to '1.4 MHz'
- dlChBw set to '3 MHz' and additionally maxNrSymPdcch < '3'
- dlChBw set to '5 MHz' and additionally maxNrSymPdcch < '2'.
(2.2) pdcchAggRarespHo must be <= '8' in the following case:
- dlChBw set to '10 MHz' and additionally maxNrSymPdcch < '2'.
(2.3) pdcchAggRarespHo must be <= '12' in all of the following cases:
- dlChBw set to '3 MHz'.
- dlChBw set to '5 MHz' and additionally maxNrSymPdcch < '3'.
- dlChBw set to '15 MHz' and additionally maxNrSymPdcch < '2'.

Conditions in (3.x) are valid in addition to (1.x) if the cellTechnology is configured to 'TDD':
(3.1) pdcchAggRarespHo must be <= '8' in the following case:
- chBw set to '10 MHz' and additionally maxNrSymPdcch < '2'.
(3.2) pdcchAggRarespHo must be <= '12' in all of the following cases:
- chBw set to '15 MHz' and additionally maxNrSymPdcch < '2'.

Conditions in (4.x) are valid if the cellTechnology of the LNCEL instance is configured to 'NB-IoT-FDD':
(4.1) pdcchAggRarespHo cannot be configured.

pdcchCqiShift.description:
The fine-tuning parameter for adjustment of measured and averaged CQI towards lower or higher aggregation in PDCCH Link Adaptation. 

The parameter gives the initial starting point for PDCCH shift dynamic control in case actOlLaPdcch is true.

The configured PDCCH CQI shift value is automatically adjusted for control channels boosting in need basis.

If actOlLaPdcch is set to 'true', pdcchCqiShift is adjusted in runtime and uses the configured value as start value.
If minPdcchCqiShift is configured, pdcchCqiShift must be greater than or equal to minPdcchCqiShift.

pdcchLoadLevel.description:
The PDCCH load level configures the percentage of used PDCCH CCEs on all available PDCCH CCEs.
Used PDCCH CCEs include all CCEs of CSS/USS space and dummy PDCCHs. 
This parameter will not restrict normal PDCCH allocation. Only when normal PDCCH load has not reach the level defined by this parameter, dummy PDCCHs will be added.
This parameter is mandatory when actPdcchLoadGen is set to "true".

pdcchUlDlBal.description:
PDCCH allocation balance initial between UL and DL for load adaptive PDCCH

The parameter determines initial value the PDCCH allocation balance constant between uplink and downlink. The Load Adaptive PDCCH algorithm optimizes the value depending on the actual load distribution between DL and UL
In fact, the PDCCH UE-specific search space capacity is divided into uplink and downlink based on the parameter before dynamic schedulings. 
The parameter pdcchUlDlBal (PDCCH LA UL DL allocation balance constant) has been originally introduced as fixed factor of split of UL and DL PDCCH resources. When Usage Based PDCCH is activated by means of parameter actLdPdcch, the pdcchUlDlBal parameter is used as an initial value of the split and as a sort of target value of the algorithm adapting the split.

Note for FDD cells:
Please note that the parameter is ignored if dlChBw is set to '1.4 MHz'.
pdcchUlDlBal.fullName: PDCCH LA UL DL allocation balance initial value
pdcchUlDlBal.notes:
Related functions: PHY/MAC Configuration (Downlink) Related parameters: LNCEL - actLdPdcch
LNCEL - cellTechnology Conditions in (1.x) are valid if the cellTechnology of the LNCEL instance is configured to 'FDD' or 'TDD':
(1.1) If actLdPdcch is set to 'false', configured UL and DL split of PDCCH resources (pdcchUlDlBal) is fixed used.
(1.2) If actLdPdcch is set to 'true', UL and DL split of PDCCH resources may be adjusted runtime based on load and the configured value (pdcchUlDlBal) defines the initial starting point then.

Conditions in (2.x) are valid in addition to (1.x) if the cellTechnology of the LNCEL instance is configured to 'TDD':
(2.1) configured pdcchUlDlBal value must be '0.1' or higher

periodicCqiFeedbackType.description:
Parameter determines if Wideband CQI or UE_selected subband CQI report mode for periodic CQI reporting on PUCCH or PUSCH should be used.
If periodicCqiFeedbackType is set to UE_selected subband CQI this means that UEs supporting subband CQI (prooved via check of FGI) use it and UEs which do not support subband CQI will use wideband CQI.

Note for the case where periodic subband CQI reporting is enabled together with DRX functionality (actDrx): 
It may not be possible to synchronize DRX start offset such that the wideband CQI report is received during the DRX OnDuration (due to periodicities) and that may cause small performance degradation in DL whenever fresh wideband channel quality information cannot be get in time. It is up to an operator whether to prevent activation of periodic subband CQI reporting and DRX in parallel because of this restriction.
periodicCqiFeedbackType.notes:
Related functions: Scheduler (Uplink) Related parameters: CAREL - lcrId
LNCEL - cellTechnology
LNCEL - cqiPerSbCycK

LNCEL_TDD - csiRepSubmode Conditions in (1.x) are valid if the cellTechnology of the LNCEL instance is configured to 'FDD' or 'TDD':
(1.1) Precondition: actDLCAggr is set to 'true'
Definitions used in below parameter relationships:
- P-LNCEL: the parent LNCEL instance of the CAREL instance
- S-LNCEL: the LNCEL instance referred by the CAREL instance having identical lcrId in the LNCEL instance
Following relationship needs to consider always two LNCEL instances, the primary (P-LNCEL) and the secondary (S-LNCEL)
- periodicCqiFeedbackType must be configured identical in P-LNCEL and the referred S-LNCEL

Conditions in (2.x) are valid in addition to (1.x) if the cellTechnology of the LNCEL instance is configured to 'FDD':
(2.1) If dlChBw is set to '1.4 MHz', periodicCqiFeedbackType must be configured to 'wideband'.
(2.2) If periodicCqiFeedbackType is set to 'UE_selected', cqiPerSbCycK must be specified.
(2.3)If dlMimoMode is set to 'Closed Loop MIMO (8x2)'  OR 'Closed Loop MIMO (8x4)' , periodicCqiFeedbackType must be set to 'wideband'.

Conditions in (3.x) are valid in addition to (1.x) if the cellTechnology of the LNCEL instance is configured to 'TDD':
(3.1) If periodicCqiFeedbackType is set to 'UE_selected' following conditions need to be fulfilled
- cqiPerSbCycK must be configured
- cqiPerSbPeriodFactor must be configured for the cell.
(3.2) csiRepSubmode must be configured in specific conditions dependent on periodicCqiFeedbackType (please refer to csiRepSubmode).

phichDur.description:
Indicates the duration of PHICH.

phichDur also puts a lower limit on the size of the control region signalled by the PCFICH. Therefore, when phichDur is set to value (Extended), three OFDMA symbols need to be enabled to for PDCCH and maxNrSymPdcch needs to be set to value 3
When phichDur is set to value (Normal), PHICH is transmitted in the first OFDMA symbol, and when phichDur is set to value (Extended), PHICH is transmitted in first three OFDMA symbols. 

phichDur is transmitted in system information as information is cell specific, and all UEs need to know whether to receive PHICH from 1 or 3 symbols. 

phichDur also puts a lower limit on the size of the control region signalled by the PCFICH. Therefore, when phichDur is set to value (Extended), three OFDMA symbols need to be enabled for PDCCH and maxNrSymPdcch needs to be set to value 3. For futher info see Table 6.9.3-1 in TS 36.211.

If phichDur is set to value 'Extended', maxNrSymPdcch in the parent LNCEL must be set to value '3'.

If phichDur is set to 'Extended', actLdPdcch in the parent LNCEL can not be configured to 'true', for phichDur set to 'Normal' the allowed value of actLdPdcch still depends on the configured values for chBw and maxNrSymPdcch.

planFileActivationMode.description:
Controls whether plan file activation is allowed to implicitly trigger eNB restart or to temporarily drop all cells('totalServiceLossAllowed') or is allowed to temporarily drop some cells('partialServiceLossAllowed') or is not allowed to temporarily drop cells ('noServiceLossAllowed')
The meaning of the activation modes is as follows:

totalServiceLossAllowed: Plan file activation is allowed to implicitly trigger eNB restart or to drop all cells if needed.

partialServiceLossAllowed: Plan file activation is not allowed to implicitly trigger eNB restart or to drop all cells but is allowed to temporarily drop some cells.

noServiceLossAllowed: Plan file activation is neither allowed to trigger eNB restart  nor to temporarily drop cells .

Dependent on the setting of the LNBTS parameter enableGrflShdn eNB will either perform direct locking of cell(s) or graceful shutdown according to the feature 'Graceful cell shut down'.

Notes:
The plan file activation mode can be overruled for a particular plan file with the LNBTS parameter forcedPlanFileActivation.

The plan file activation mode is ignored in case of autoconfiguration respectively commissioning of an uncommissioned eNB and in case of full commissioing via BTS Site Manager. Such plan files will be activated in any case.

The feature ‘Automatic lock' shall be activated, i.e. the parameter LNBTS-enableAutoLock shall be set to ‘enabled’ (which is the default value). Otherwise the plan file would be rejected by eNB if cell dropping is needed.
planFileActivationMode.notes: Related functions: BTS Site or Cell Configuration
planFileActivationMode.relatedFeatures: •  LTE2060 Addition or replacement of radios without site outage (Standard)
planFileActivationMode.source: Nokia SBTS 18A official SingleRAN AirScale parameter dictionary

plrAlarmThreshold.description:
This parameter defines the threshold, in %, for raising the TWAMP session alarm for reasons of excessive packet loss ratio (PLR).
The alarm is raised if the packet loss ratio observed over a 15-minute evaluation period equals or exceeds the threshold value. The alarm will be cleared if the packet loss ratio drops below the threshold value for two consecutive 15-minute observation periods.
Setting PLR Threshold to the maximum value (100%) is valid but not recommended. An alarm would be triggered only in extreme cases, e.g. when "the line is cut" or "the reflector at peer end is gone".
plrAlarmThreshold.relatedFeatures:

portDefaultPriority.description:

Every untagged ingress Ethernet frame at this interface gets assigned this Port Default Priority. If QoS classification mode is configured to VLAN-PCP, this priority is used for enqueing decision of the frame. If the frame egresses the switch tagged, this priority shall be used in the VLAN tag header.

portDefaultVlanId.description:
This parameter defines the VLAN identifier that is associated to untagged and priority-tagged frames received at this Ethernet interface (internal switch-port).

Furthermore this parameter determines, that frames associated to this VLAN identifier which are switched and transmitted at this switch-port will be transmitted untagged.

In order to achieve that a received untagged or priority-tagged frame is switched and transmitted via another (external) switch-port, the same VLAN identifier must be configured at the transmission port:
a) for VLAN-tagged transmission: in the VLAN identifier list of that transmit switch-port (see parameter l2VlanIdList) or
b) for untagged transmission: in the portDefaultVlanID of that transmit switch-port.
Else the frame will be discarded.
portDefaultVlanId.fullName: Default VLAN identifier for layer 2 switching
portDefaultVlanId.notes: Related parameters: BRGPRT - l2VlanIdList In order that the frame will be transmitted via another Ethernet interface, after layer 2 switching has been performed, the same VLAN id must be configured in the VLAN identifier list of that Ethernet interface.
portDefaultVlanId.relatedFeatures:

•  RC0249 Porting of legacy transport features for Cloud BTS (Standard)

portDefaultVlanPriority.description:
This parameter defines the default VLAN priority assigned to untagged Ethernet frames received at this Ethernet interface (external switch-port)

The priority is used:
- for QoS classification of the frame, depending on the selected qosClassificationCriteria and frame content,
- for L2 priority marking of the frame at egress when the frame is transmitted VLAN-tagged, depending on the transmit port VLAN configuration.

The priority level values range from zero (best effort) to seven (highest).

prachFreqOff.description:
Defines the location in frequency for the PRACH transmissions.
For UL scheduling its recommended that PRACH is located next to PUCCH either on the lower or upper edge of the bandwidth because UL PRB allocation for UE consist of consecutive PRBs. If there is a small gap between PUCCH and PRACH PRBs, UL scheduler cannot utilize those PRBs effectively. prachFreqOffset for each bandwidth should be set aligned with the parameters determining the number of PRBs for PUCCH, so that PRACH is located next to PUCCH.
It is recommended to set the value such that PRACH does not overlap with PUCCH RBs and is located adjacent to PUCCH; thus recommended parameter alternatives are: 
1) roundup((MaxPucchResourceSize+blankedPucch)/2) if it is located at the lower edge, or
2) ulChBw(in PRBs)-6-roundup((MaxPucchResourceSize+blankedPucch)/2 ) if it is located at the upper edge of the PUSCH area

The MaxPucchResourceSize in above defines the maximum number of allocated PUCCH RBs, and it defined in nCqiRb parameter.
prachFreqOff.notes:
Related functions: PRACH / RACH configuration Related parameters: LNCEL_FDD - actAutoPucchAlloc
LNCEL_FDD - blankedPucch
LNCEL_FDD - selectOuterPuschRegion
LNCEL_FDD - ulChBw

SLCOMMRES - scTFResConfigPrbNum
SLCOMMRES - scTFResConfigPrbStart Conditions listed below are only applicable if actAutoPucchAlloc is set to 'false'.

(1)
(1.1) For ulChBw of '3MHz', '5 MHz', '10 MHz', '15 MHz' and '20 MHz': 
if selectOuterPuschRegion is configured to 'None' or blankedPucch is less than '12', then the allowed prachFreqOff range is:
roundup ((MaxPucchResourceSize + blankedPucch) / 2) … ulChBw (in PRBs) - 6 - roundup ((MaxPucchResourceSize + blankedPucch) / 2)

(1.2) For ulChBw of '5 MHz', '10 MHz', '15 MHz' and '20 MHz': 
- if selectOuterPuschRegion is configured to 'LowerEdge' and blankedPucch is greater than or equal to '12', then the allowed prachFreqOff ranges are:
   + (0 ... roundup (blankedPucch/2) - 6) and 
   + (roundup ((MaxPucchResourceSize + blankedPucch) / 2) … ulChBw (in PRBs) - 6 - roundup ((MaxPucchResourceSize + blankedPucch) / 2))
- if selectOuterPuschRegion is configured to 'UpperEdge' and blankedPucch is greater than or equal to '12', then the allowed prachFreqOff ranges are:
   + (roundup ((MaxPucchResourceSize + blankedPucch) / 2) … ulChBw (in PRBs) - 6 - roundup ((MaxPucchResourceSize + blankedPucch) / 2)) and 
   + ((ulChBw(in PRBs) – roundup (blankedPuccch/2)) ... ulChBw(in PRBs) – 6)

Note: MaxPucchResourceSize is calculated in nCqiRb.

(2) If ulChBw is set to '1.4 MHz', prachFreqOff must be configured to 0.

(3) PRACH allocation (prachFreqOff) and PUSCH mask allocation (ulsPuschMask) must be mutually exclusive, ie. the range {prachFreqOff .. (prachFreqOff+5)} must not be within the PUSCH mask range(s) {ulsPuschMaskStart .. (ulsPuschMaskStart+ulsPuschMaskLength-1)}

In addition the conditions for ProSe sidelink configuration apply, see parameter  SLCOMMRES-scTFResConfigPrbEnd, SLCOMMRES-scTFResConfigPrbNum, SLCOMMRES-scTFResConfigPrbStart, SLCOMMRES-dataTFResConfigPrbEnd, SLCOMMRES-dataTFResConfigPrbNum, SLCOMMRES-dataTFResConfigPrbStart.

preventPsHOtoWcdma.description:
This parameter can be used to generally prevent the execution of PS-handover towards WCDMA for all UE or to prevent the execution of PS-handover towards WCDMA for all UE without an active VoIP bearer.
If this parameter is set to "All" all UE will be sent to WCDMA by UE Context Release with redirect, even if the UE would be able to perform handover.
If this parameter is set to "NonVoiceOnly" all UE without an established VoIP bearer will be sent to WCDMA by UE Context Release with redirect, even if the UE would be able to perform handover.
This parameter must be configured if handover to WCDMA is activated. It is not needed otherwise.

prioTopoHO.description:
This parameter is used to define priorities between the 3 topology options for intra LTE handover, which are 
1) Intra eNB HO
2) HO via X2
3) HO via S1
It's assumed that Intra eNB HO can not have lower priority than any other topology and S1 HO can not have higher priority than any other topology.

Four relations are possible:
1) all topologies have the same priority -> "all equal"
2) intra eNB HO is prioritized over inter eNB HO where X2-based HO and S1-based HO are not discriminated -> "intra eNB HO prior inter eNB HO"
3) intra eNB HO is prioritized over inter eNB HO where X2-based HO is prioritized over S1-based HO -> "intra prior X2 prior S1"
4) intra eNB HO and X2-based handover are not discriminated but S1-based HO takes lower priority than the others -> "low prio S1"
prioTopoHO.range:
0: all equal 
1: intra eNB HO prior inter eNB HO 
2: intra prior X2 prior S1 
3: low prio S1
prioTopoHO.source: Nokia SBTS 18A official SingleRAN AirScale parameter dictionary

probFac.description:
Defines the maximum barring threshold and  probability for a UE to establish an RRC connection.
The access probability factor defines the probability for a UE to establish an RRC connection.
The UE draws a random number (0 <= rand < 1). If rand is higher than the value indicated by the access probability factor, the UE considers the access barring check to be unsuccessful.
probFac.fullName: Max auto access probability factor for CS fallback
probFac.notes:
Related parameters: ACBPR - acBarCsfbOcAutoMax-barAC
ACBPR - acBarCsfbOcAutoMin-probFac If acBarCsfbOcAutoMax-barAC has any bits for AC11 to 15 set to 1 then acBarCsfbOcAutoMax-probFac can take only value 0%. With this restriction, values other than 0% for acBarCsfbOcAutoMax-probFac can only be set if all bits of the corresponding acBarCsfbOcAutoMax-barAC are set to 0.

acBarCsfbOcAutoMax-probFac must be less than or equal to acBarCsfbOcAutoMin-probFac.
probFac.source: Nokia SBTS 18A official SingleRAN AirScale parameter dictionary

prohibitLBHOTimer.description:
This timer is used for temporary blacklisting of a Target Cell for load-based and service-based handover.
One Target Cell is blacklisted when a handover is rejected because of lack of resources.
The timer is started when the cell is blacklisted.
When timer expires the blacklisting is removed.
Blacklist affects all UEs in the actual source cell.
Blacklist affects Handovers for Load Balancing. (cause "Reduce Load in Serving Cell" ) and Service Based Handovers (cause "Resource Optimisation Handover")
Blacklisted cells are managed internally by eNB and not added to black lists visible to operator.

protocol.description:
This parameter defines the protocol information of the IP packet.
If the parameter has value -1, the policy is valid for all protocols.
The value 0...254 refers to the protocol number in the IP header.

- single IP address (equivalent to netmask /32 in IPv4), no particular protocol/port 
- single IP address, selected protocol/port
- IP subnet, no particular protocol/port
- IP subnet, selected protocol/port.

prsConfigurationIndex.description:
Determines the periodicity and offset of the PRS occasions for FDD

PRS period based on the configured value of prsConfigurationIndex:
7, 14, 27, 47, 67, 87, 107, 127, 147, 151: 160 ms period
471: 320 ms period
1111: 640 ms period
2391: 1280 ms period
The periodicity and offset can be computed according to 3GPP TS 36.211 Rel9

Note: All Cat-M UEs in RRC Connected mode may be released when this parameter is online modified.
prsConfigurationIndex.notes:
Related functions: Location Services Related parameters: LNBTS - actCMAS
LNBTS - actETWS
LNBTS - actMBMS
LNCEL - actOtdoa
LNCEL - cellTechnology
LNCEL - prsNumDlFrames
LNCEL_FDD - dlChBw
LNCEL_FDD - earfcnDL
MBSFNSYNCAREA_FDD - mbsfnDlChBw
MBSFNSYNCAREA_FDD - mbsfnEarfcn This parameter must be configured if actOtdoa is set to 'true'.

If prsConfigurationIndex is set to a value >= 151, the following conditions (1) to (3) must be fulfilled:

(1a)  If (actCMAS or actETWS or sib2xTransmit is set to 'true') AND actOtdoa is set to 'true' AND the number of configured SIBs (i.e. the number of sets in structure sibSchedulingList + 2) is 7 or smaller, then prsConfigurationIndex must be set to one of the following values:  '151', '471', '1111' or '2391'.
(1b)  If (actCMAS or actETWS or sib2xTransmit is set to 'true') AND actOtdoa is set to 'true' AND siWindowLen is set to '20 ms' AND the number of configured SIBs (i.e. the number of sets in structure sibSchedulingList + 2) is 8 or higher then prsConfigurationIndex must be set to one of the following values: '471', '1111' or '2391'. 

(2) If (actCMAS or actETWS or sib2xTransmit is set to 'true') AND actOtdoa is set to 'true' AND siWindowLen is set to '40 ms' AND the number of configured SIBs (i.e. the number of sets in structure sibSchedulingList + 2) is 8 or higher then prsConfigurationIndex must be set to one of the following values: '1111' or '2391'. 

(3) prsConfigurationIndex is limited in its allowed values in following conditions:
(3.1) If dlMimoMode is set to ('Closed Loop MIMO (4x2)' OR 'Closed Loop MIMO (4x4)' OR 'Closed Loop MIMO (8x2)' OR 'Closed Loop MIMO (8x4)') AND activatedMimoTM is NOT set to 'TM4'
(3.1.1) ... AND (the number of configured SIBs (i.e. the number of sets in structure sibSchedulingList + 2) is >= 8)
(3.1.1.1) … AND (siWindowLen is set to '40ms')
- prsConfigurationIndex must be configured to one of the following values: '1111', '2391'.
(3.1.1.2) … AND (siWindowLen is not set to '40ms')
- prsConfigurationIndex must be configured to one of the following values: '471', '1111', '2391'.

 If prsConfigurationIndex is set to a value < 151, the following conditions (4) to (7) must be fulfilled 
(4) if (actCMAS or actETWS or sib2xTransmit) is 'true' AND actOtdoa is set to 'true' and dlChBw > '5 MHz' then prsNumDlFrames must be set to 1.
(5) if dlChBw = '5 MHz', then if prsConfigurationIndex is set to '7, 27, 47, 67, 87, 107, 127, 147' then prsNumDlFrames can be set to 2 only if actEicic is 'false'
(6) if prsConfigurationIndex is set to '14', prsNumDlFrames must be set to 1.
(7) The allowed values of csiRsConfigInfo-csiRsSubfrConf depends on prsConfigurationIndex and prsNumDlFrames. Please refer to csiRsSubfrConf for details.

For any value of prsConfigurationIndex, the following (8) and (9) apply:

(8) If actMBMS is set to 'true', for each LNCEL containing MBSFNCEL, where LNCEL_FDD-earfcnDL equal to MBSFNSYNCAREA_FDD-mbsfnEarfcn and LNCEL_FDD-dlChBw equal to MBSFNSYNCAREA_FDD-mbsfnDlChBw, LNCEL_FDD-prsConfigurationIndex must be set to a value from the same set of the following four mutually exclusive sets: [14], [151, 471, 1111, 2391], [7, 47, 87, 127], [27, 67, 107, 147].

(9) if nbIoTMode is set to 'inband' and cellTechnology is set to 'FDD',prsConfigurationIndex value limited as below.
(9.1) prsConfigurationIndex must not be set 14.
(9.2) prsConfigurationIndex must not be set 153,1113,2393 when prsNumDlFrames set to 2

prsNumDlFrames.notes:
Related functions: Location Services Related parameters: LNCEL - actOtdoa
LNCEL_TDD - csiRsConfigInfo-csiRsSubfrConf

(4.1) If tddFrameConf is set to '1' (sa1), prsNumDlFrames must be set to '1'.
(4.2) If tddFrameConf is set to '2' (sa2), prsNumDlFrames is not limited.

prsPowerBoost.description:
Power Boosting for PRS increases hearability and allows for a more flexible use of the DL Tx power.

With de-boosting it is possible to lower PRS power in interference sensitive areas.
PRS power is related to DL RS power, and when prsPowerBoost is set to value 0dB, and dlRsBoost is set to same 0dB value, PRS and DL RS has same power in each TX Antenna. 

Note also the case when actPrsTxDiv is TRUE. Power is same in each TX Antenna, but as PRS is transmitted at the same time from each used TX Antenna, sum of PRS power over all TX Antennas are higher. To compensate power in TxDiv case, prsPowerBoost can be set to proper value. See examples below:

Example 1:
dlMimoMode is set to TxDiv, value -3 dB sets the sum of PRS power to equal to DL RS power.

Example 2:
dlMimoMode is set to 4-way TxDiv, value -6 dB sets the sum of PRS power to equal to DL RS power.

Example 3:
dlMimoMode is set to Closed Loop MIMO (4x2), value -3 dB sets the sum of PRS power to equal to DL RS power.
prsPowerBoost.notes: Related functions: Location Services Related parameters: LNCEL - actOtdoa prsPowerBoost is mandatory required if actOtdoa is set to 'true'.
prsPowerBoost.relatedFeatures:
•  LTE495 OTDOA (Optional)  
•  LTE568 DL adaptive closed loop MIMO (4x2) (Optional)

pucchF3Support2CC.description:
This parameter configures the PUCCH format 3 support for 2CC CA configurations for TDD cells.
If the value is configured to 'true' the BTS uses 4 PF3 PRBs at cell setup. If the parameter is configured to value 'false' the BTS won’t configure any PF3 PRB at cell setup. 
In the case of 3CC CA, the BTS always uses fixed 4 PF3 PRBs.

The parameter is applicable for FSMF as well as AirScale.

pucchF3Support2CC.relatedFeatures: •  LTE2615 Extended CQI period for high capacity cells (Standard)

pureRrcPreempPrioNB.description:
This parameter indicates ARP priority of preempting NB-IoT RRC connection contexts without established DRBs.
The value '15' (no priority) indicates that pure NB-IoT RRC connections will not be selected for preemptions, i.e., LTE4739 for NB-IoT part is disabled.
The value '16' (LowestPrioAboveSCell) indicates that pure NB-IoT RRC connections will be selected for preemption before any wideband UE and only if no SCell context is available.
The value '17' (LowestPrioBelowSCell) indicates that pure NB-IoT RRC connections will be selected for preemption before any wideband UE and before any SCell context.
pureRrcPreempPrioNB.fullName: Preemption priority of pure NB-IoT RRC connections
pureRrcPreempPrioNB.notes:
Related functions: Radio Admission Control Related parameters: LNBTS - actContextPreemption
LNCEL - cellTechnology pureRrcPreempPrioNB can be configured to value other than ‘15’ only if all of the following conditions are fulfilled:
- actContextPreemption is set to 'true';
- cellTechnology of at least one LNCELL instance is set to 'NB-IoT-FDD'.
pureRrcPreempPrioNB.relatedFeatures: •   LTE4739 Cat-M/NB-IoT UE context and bearer preemption (Standard)

pwsWithEmAreaId.description:
Indicates if the Public Warning Systems (ETWS and/or CMAS) make use of Emergency Area IDs. 
If ETWS or CMAS service is activated, then provision of this parameter is mandatory.

If 'pwsWithEmAreaId' is true, then for each eNB cell provision of at least one 'Emergency Area ID' in the 'emAreaIdList' must be specified. 

If a warning message including 'Emergency Area IDs' is received by eNB and 'pwsWithEmAreaId' is 'false' then this warning message shall not be broadcasted by eNB.
pwsWithEmAreaId.notes:
Related functions: RAN Common Signalling Related parameters: LNBTS - actCMAS
LNBTS - actETWS
LNBTS_FDD - actUnlicensedAcc
LNCEL - emAreaIdList
LNCEL_FDD - earfcnDL pwsWithEmAreaId must be configured if at least one of the parameters actETWS or actCMAS is set to 'true'. 

Conditions in (1.x) are valid if the supportedCellTechnology of the LNBTS instance is configured to 'FDD' or 'mixed_FDD_TDD' and applicable to all cells with cellTechnology set to 'FDD':
(1.1) if pwsWithEmAreaId is set to 'true' AND 
(1.1.1) earfcnDL is NOT from unlicensed band as defined in parameter actUnlicensedAcc, the emAreaIdList must be configured with at least one item per LNCEL instance.
(1.1.2) earfcnDL IS from unlicensed band as defined in parameter actUnlicensedAcc and actUnlicensedAcc is 'LAA', the emAreaIdList must be configured empty per LNCEL instance.
pwsWithEmAreaId.relatedFeatures:
•  LTE843 ETWS broadcast (Optional)  
•  LTE494 Commercial Mobile Alert System (Optional)  
•  LTE1755 Multiple emergency areas per cell (Standard)  
•  LTE2860 Licensed-Assisted Access (Standard)

qci1DrxOffThreshold.description:
Threshold for the poor radio condition when DRX will be disabled for UEs using VoLTE (QCI1 bearer configured).
This threshold is defined in terms of CQI. If DRX is enabled for a VoLTE UE, and the VoLTE UE’s corrected CQI value remains below this threshold for a sufficient amount of time, then DRX will be disabled for the UE.
qci1DrxOffThreshold.notes:
Related functions: DRX (Control & Basic DRX Profile) Related parameters: DRX - qci1DrxOnThreshold
LNCEL - actQci1RfDrx If actQci1RfDrx is 'true' then qci1DrxOffThreshold must be configured.
qci1DrxOffThreshold must be smaller than qci1DrxOnThreshold.
qci1DrxOffThreshold.source: Nokia SBTS 18A official SingleRAN AirScale parameter dictionary

qci1DrxOnThreshold.description:

qosClassification.defaultValue: DSCP (0) (Default value means DSCP to PHB mapping.)
qosClassification.description:
This parameter specifies if the layer 2 switching is based on DSCP to PHB mapping or on PCP to PHB mapping.
- In case it is DSCP to PHB mapping, the queue for egress traffic is taken from parameter dscpMap for IP frames and from parameter priorityQueueNonIP for non-IP frames.
- In case it is PCP to PHB mapping, the queue for egress traffic is taken from the parameters priorityQueuePcp0 to priorityQueuePcp7 for tagged frames and from parameter priorityQueueUntagged for untagged frames.
qosClassification.source: Nokia LTE18 official BTS parameter dictionary (FDD)

qosClassificationCriteria.description:
This parameter defines the criteria to be used for the egress QoS classification for all switch-ports (i.e. criteria for the enqueuing decision).

Depending on the criteria, the actual mapping of values must be defined in 
managed object classes PCP2QMAP and DSCPTOQMAP or the parameter vlanIdToQueueMap.

raRespWinSize.description:
Random Access Response Window Size parameter defines the window size for the random access response in TTIs.

Notes: 
For FDD cells if eICIC feature is activated a value higher than default 7 is recommended to be used.

For TDD cells with ...
- Preamble format 0:
If the UL/DL configuration is 1 then the raRespWindowSize must be set to a value greater than or equal to 5.
If the UL/DL configuration is 2 then the raRespWindowSize must be set to a value greater than or equal to 4.
- Preamble format 1:
If the UL/DL configuration is 1 and the special subframe configuration is 5 then the raRespWindowSize must be set to a value greater than or equal to 4.
- Preamble format 2:
If the UL/DL configuration is 1 and the special subframe configuration is 5 then the raRespWindowSize must be set to a value greater than or equal to 4.
- Preamble format 4:
If the UL/DL configuration is 1 and the special subframe configuration is 7 then the raRespWindowSize must be set to a value greater than or equal to 3.
If the UL/DL configuration is 1 and the special subframe configuration is 5 then the raRespWindowSize must be set to a value greater than or equal to 6.
If the UL/DL configuration is 2 and the special subframe configuration is 7 then the raRespWindowSize must be set to a value greater than or equal to 3.
If the UL/DL configuration is 2 and the special subframe configuration is 5 then the raRespWindowSize must be set to a value greater than or equal to 5.
raRespWinSize.notes:
Related functions: PRACH / RACH configuration Related parameters: LNBTS - actDLUnicastMbsfn
LNBTS - actMBMS
LNBTS_FDD - actFlexBbUsage
LNCEL - actEicic
LNCEL - actMicroDtx
LNCEL - cellTechnology
LNCEL_FDD - ulChBw
LNCEL_TDD - prachConfIndex
LNCEL_TDD - tddSpecSubfConf
MBSFNSYNCAREA_FDD - maxSyncSubfrPShare
MBSFNSYNCAREA_TDD - maxSyncSubfrPShare Conditions in (1.x) are valid if the cellTechnology of the LNCEL instance is configured to 'FDD':
(1.1) If actFlexBbUsage is set to 'true' AND and (ulChBw,dlChBw) has value '5 MHz' or '10 MHz, raRespWinSize must be configured to value '10'.
(1.2) If ulChBw is set to '1.4 MHz', raRespWinSize is not allowed to be configured to be less than '5'.
(1.3) If actEicic is set to 'true', raRespWinSize must be set to a value greater than or equal to '6'.
(1.4) If actMBMS is equal to 'true' 
(1.4.1) ... AND maxSyncSubfrPShare in MBSFNSYNCAREA_FDD is less than or equal to 30%, raRespWinSize must be greater than or equal to 6 .
(1.4.2) ...AND maxSyncSubfrPShare in MBSFNSYNCAREA_FDD is greater than 30% AND less than or equal to 40%, raRespWinSize must be greater than or equal to 8 .
(1.4.3) ...AND maxSyncSubfrPShare in MBSFNSYNCAREA_FDD is greater than 40%, raRespWinSize must be greater than or equal to 10 .
(1.5) actMicroDtx can only be set to 'true' if raRespWinSize is set to '8' or higher.
(1.6) if (actDLUnicastMbsfn is equal to 'true') AND 
(1.6.1) uMbsfnShareMax is less than or equal to 30%, then raRespWinSize must be greater than or equal '6'.
(1.6.2) uMbsfnShareMax greater than 30% AND less than or equal to 40%, then raRespWinSize must be greater than or equal to '8'.
(1.6.3) uMbsfnShareMax is greater than 40%, then raRespWinSize must be greater than or equal to '10'


Conditions in (2.x) are valid if the cellTechnology of the LNCEL instance is configured to 'TDD':
(2.1) If prachConfIndex is 3...7 (preamble format 0)
(2.1.1) ... AND tddFrameConf is '1'(sa1), raRespWinSize should be set to a value greater than or equal to 5.
(2.1.2) ... AND tddFrameConf is '2'(sa2), raRespWinSize should be set to a value greater than or equal to 4.
(2.2) If prachConfIndex is 23...25 (preamble format 1) or 33...35 (preamble format 2) AND tddFrameConf is '1'(sa1) AND tddSpecSubfConf is '5' (ssp5), raRespWinSize should be set to a value greater than or equal to 4
(2.3) If prachConfIndex is 51...53 (preamble format 4) AND tddFrameConf is '1'(sa1) 
(2.3.1) ... AND tddSpecSubfConf is '5' (ssp5), raRespWinSize should be set to a value greater than or equal to 6
(2.3.2) ... AND tddSpecSubfConf is '7' (ssp7), raRespWinSize should be set to a value greater than or equal to 3
(2.4) If prachConfIndex is 51...53 (preamble format 4) AND tddFrameConf is '2'(sa2) 
(2.4.1) ... AND tddSpecSubfConf is '5' (ssp5), raRespWinSize should be set to a value greater than or equal to 5
(2.4.2) ... AND tddSpecSubfConf is '7' (ssp5), raRespWinSize should be set to a value greater than or equal to 3.
(2.5) If actMBMS is equal to 'true' 
(2.5.1) ... AND maxSyncSubfrPShare in MBSFNSYNCAREA_TDD is less than or equal to 18.75%, raRespWinSize must be greater than or equal to 6
(2.5.2) ... AND maxSyncSubfrPShare in MBSFNSYNCAREA_TDD is greater than 18.75%, raRespWinSize must be greater than or equal to 10 .
(2.6) If actMicroDtx is set to 'true', raRespWinSize must be set to '10' or higher.
(2.7) If actEicic is set to 'true', raRespWinSize must be set to a value greater than or equal to '10'.

This parameter selects whether Target eNodeB shall provide and reserve a dedicated RACH preamble for HO from UTRAN. 
In case no dedicated RACH preamble is provided UE will perform contention based RACH access.
If a dedicated RACH preamble is provided UE will perform non-contention based RACH access as for intra LTE handover.

In this case contention based RACH access will be used as fallback solution.

radioMemAbnormalThreshold.description:
This parameter defines the abnormal memory threshold on the radio module.
When the memory consumption on the radio module exceeds the abnormal threshold, an alarm with fault ‘Radio memory consumption exceeds abnormal threshold’ is  raised. When the memory consumption on the radio module falls below the abnormal threshold, the alarm with fault ‘Radio memory consumption exceeds abnormal threshold’ is cleared.
This parameter is defined as a relative value, where the lower bound value of 0% indicates expected average memory consumption.
When abnormal memory threshold is set to 100%, the alarm with fault ‘Radio memory consumption exceeds abnormal threshold’ is not raised and alarm with fault ‘Radio memory consumption exceeds critical threshold’ is directly raised.

radioProtSearchOrder.description:
This parameter allows the operator to define the starting protocol for radio detection between OBSAI and CPRI variants.  

When this parameter is set, the FHS will start the radio protocol detection algorithm with the specified protocol on first startup or following upgrade activation of that module.  The use of this parameter can reduce the radio detection time in configurations where the Operator knows the type of radio deployment. If this parameter is not specified, the FHS will still be able to automatically detect the type of radio protocols in use, although the time to detect the radios may be increased for certain exceptional cases.  In this scenario, the FHS will attempt to use prior radio detection information to select the starting point for protocol searches.

Since this parameter defines the starting point for the search algorithm, it can only decrease the detection time for radios that are attached to the FHS when the algorithm is started. If no radios are attached to the module, the time to detect to the radios will be dependent upon the radio protocol type and the current protocol being probed by the FHS.

Note that if the Operator sets this parameter incorrectly, the radio detection time can be increased following a BTS restart or upgrade activation.

In all scenarios, the BTS will be able to detect the radio protocol with or without the Operator’s use of this parameter.

redBwMaxRbUl.description:
Defines the maximum number of PRBs which may be assigned to a UE scheduled in UL when restricted PRB assignment in uplink is enabled.
Note that the actual amount of PRBs in UL allocation must be of the form 2^i*3^j*5^k where i, j and k are non-negative integers, so effectively the value will be rounded down to the next value complying with the rule.

Please note that the default value is not suitable for all bandwidths. The recommended values are:
- if ulChBw is set to '1.4 MHz':6
- if ulChBw is set to '3 MHz': 15
- if ulChBw is set to '5 MHz': 25
- if ulChBw is set to '10 MHz': 50
- if ulChBw is set to '15 MHz': 75
- if ulChBw is set to '20 MHz':100
redBwMaxRbUl.fullName: Maximum number of PRBs assigned in uplink
redBwMaxRbUl.notes:
Related functions: Scheduler (Uplink) Related parameters: LNCEL - cellTechnology
LNCEL_FDD - ulChBw
LNCEL_TDD - chBw Conditions in (1.x) are valid if the cellTechnology of the LNCEL instance is configured to 'FDD':
(1.1) The maximal value of redBwMaxRbUl depends on the ulChBw:
- for ulChBw set to '1.4 MHz', redBwMaxRbUl is restricted to 1.. 6
- for ulChBw set to '3 MHz', redBwMaxRbUl is restricted to 1.. 15
- for ulChBw set to '5MHz',  redBwMaxRbUl is restricted to 1.. 25
- for ulChBw set to '10MHz',  redBwMaxRbUl is restricted to 1.. 50
- for ulChBw set to '15MHz',  redBwMaxRbUl is restricted to 1.. 75
- for ulChBw set to '20MHz',  redBwMaxRbUl is not limited

Conditions in (2.x) are valid if the cellTechnology of the LNCEL instance is configured to 'TDD':

redBwMinRbUl.description:
Defines the minimum number of PRBs which may be assigned to a UE scheduled in UL when restricted PRB assignment in uplink is enabled. However, a lower number of PRBs is allowed if the transport block size with this number of PRBs and the MCS selected by AMC would exceed the UE capabilities.

- redirGeranBandIndicator must be configured
- at least one of the following conditions must be fulfilled in this REDRT
  * emerCallPrio must be configured 
  * csFallBPrio must be configured
  * redirectPrio must be configured
(1.4) If redirRat is set to 'cdma2000HRPD' following configuration is needed
- redirBandCdma must be configured
- redirFreqCdma must be configured
- redirectPrio must be configured
(1.5) If redirRat is set to 'cdma20001xRTT' following configuration is needed
- redirBandCdma must be configured
- redirFreqCdma must be configured
- at least one of the following conditions must be fulfilled in this REDRT
  * emerCallPrio must be configured 
  * csFallBPrio must be configured
  * redirectPrio must be configured
(1.6) If actGsmRedirWithSI is set to 'true', redirRat can be set to 'geran' only if additionally the parameter addGsmSIToRedirMsg is set.
For actGsmRedirWithSI set to 'false' the configuiration for redirRat is not restricted.
(1.7) If act1xCsfb is set to 'true' and additionally for the LNCEL instance rttCsfbType is not set to 'forbidden' all of the following condition need to be fulfilled
- at least one instance of REDRT with redirRAT 'cdma20001xRTT' must be created for this LNCEL with csFallBPrio configured
- at least one instance of REDRT with redirRAT 'cdma20001xRTT' must be created for the cell with emerCallPrio configured
- for any additional REDRT instance belonging to the LNCEL when redirRat is set to 'cdma20001xRTT', at least one of csFallBPrio, emerCallPrio or redirectPrio must be configured.

Conditions in (2.x) are valid in addition to (1.x) if the cellTechnology of the parent LNCEL instance is configured to 'FDD':
(2.1) redirRat can not be configured to 'utraTDD'

Conditions in (3.x) are valid in addition to (1.x) if the cellTechnology of the parent LNCEL instance is configured to 'TDD':
(3.1) If redirRat is set to  'utraTDD' following configuration is needed
- redirFreqUtraTDDL must be configured
- at least one of the following conditions must be fulfilled in this REDRT instance
  * emerCallPrio must be configured 
  * csFallBPrio must be configured
  * redirectPrio must be configured.

remoteSyslogServerIPaddress.description:
This parameter holds the IP address of the remote syslog server.

The interface is disabled by setting the IP address to ""0.0.0.0"".

For IPv4, the parameter has to be entered in dotted decimal format.

For IPv6, the parameter has to be entered according to formats specified in RFC4291. 

IPv4 address ranges:
It is not allowed to configure the broadcast address 255.255.255.255 or an address within the range of multicast addresses
(224.0.0.0-239.255.255.255) or loop-back addresses (127.0.0.0-127.255.255.255).

IPv6 address ranges:
It is recommended to configure only an address within the range of Unique Local Unicast addresses (FC00::/7) or Global Unicast addresses (2000::/3).
remoteSyslogServerIPaddress.notes: Related functions: Site Management (Troubleshooting) Related parameters: MNL/MNLENT/FEATCADM/FEATLADM - actDualStackIpV4V6ForMplane If actDualStackIpV4V6ForMplane=false, this must be set in IPv4 format only.

rfSharingEnabled.description:
This parameter enables RF sharing with GSM, UTRAN, or EUTRA (FDD or TDD) between BTSs.

The shared RF cannot  be chained.
The shared ASIRMODs can be chained.

When RP3-01 sync is used between LTE and 3G,
LTE-3G RF sharing can be configured only if the shared BTS does or will contain a 3G System Module. If the 3G System Module does not exist and the LTE-3G RF sharing has been configured, LTE BTS will stay in the initializing state because the 3G System Module is always the synchronization master in case of LTE-3G RF sharing. Initializing state in the LTE BTS SW prevents reconfiguration commissioning of the LTE BTS by the BTS Site Manager.

When Sync Hub Direct Forward is used, and the LTE is the sync slave,
LTE-3G or LTE-LTE RF sharing can be configured only if the shared BTS does or will contain another 3G/LTE System Module. If the 3G/ LTE System Module does not exist and the LTE-3G or LTE-LTE RF sharing has been configured, LTE BTS will stay in the initializing state when the shared 3G/LTE System Module is the synch hub master or it is disrupting the synchronization chain. Initializing state in the LTE BTS SW prevents reconfiguration commissioning of the LTE BTS by the BTS Site Manager.

When LTE-LTE + LTE-GSM is configured, Sync Hub Direct Forward must be used. The LTE sync slave can be configured only if the shared BTS does or will contain another LTE or GSM System Module which provides sync propagation. If the LTE or GSM System Module does not exist, the LTE-LTE + LTE-GSM RF sharing has been configured, and the position of the LTE BTS in the SHDF chain is after a module that does not exist, that is, forwarded synch not provided, the LTE BTS will stay in the initializing state. Initializing state in the LTE BTS SW prevents reconfiguration commissioning of the LTE BTS by the BTS Site Manager. 

When AirScale is used, Sync Hub Direct Forward must be used.

When operating in RF sharing mode, a single RF Module is connected to two modules (System or Baseband Extension) simultaneously.

Two technologies are connected to the one and the same Flexi Multiradio RF Module. The two technologies can be:
- Flexi EDGE System Module is operating in GSM/EDGE SW with Flexi Multimode System Module in LTE
- Flexi EDGE System Module is operating in GSM/EDGE SW with Flexi Baseband Extension Module in LTE
- Flexi Multimode System Module is operating in WCDMA SW with Flexi Multimode System Module in LTE
- Flexi Multimode System Module is operating in WCDMA SW with Flexi Baseband Extension Module in LTE
- Flexi Multimode System/Extension Module is operating in LTE SW with a Flexi Multimode System/Extension Module in the peer LTE (LTE-LTE RF sharing) 

Two technologies are connected to the one and the same ASIRMOD. The two technologies can be:
- Flexi Baseband Extension Module in LTE TDD with Flexi Baseband Extension Module in LTE FDD

When the parameter ""rfSharingEnabled"" is ""true"" and LTE-LTE RF sharing is configured with additional sharing with GSM, the following are the recommended Sync Hub configuration:
1st in chain - LTE
2nd in chain – LTE
3rd in chain - GSM
4th in chain – GSM
When the parameter ""rfSharingEnabled"" is ""true"" and LTE-LTE RF sharing is configured without additional sharing with GSM, the parameter ""BTSSCL-syncPropagationEnabled"" must be set to ""true"" in one BTS and ""false"" in the other BTS.

The BTS will dynamically decide if a BTS restart or dropping of cells is needed.
rfSharingEnabled.notes:
Related functions: Site Management (System Management) Related parameters: CABLINK - firstEndpointDN
CABLINK - secondEndpointDN
LNBTS - supportedCellTechnology
RMOD - cpriARfSharing
SMOD_EXT - eutraSupport
SMOD_EXT - eutraTDDSupport
SMOD_EXT - geranSupport rfSharingEnabled can be set to value 'true' only when one of the following is true:
1. supportedCellTechnology contains 'FDD'
2. supportedCellTechnology contains 'TDD' and shared module is ASIRMOD

When rfSharingEnabled is set to value 'false'. There shall not be any SMOD_EXT instance created for RF sharing purposes.

When rfSharingEnabled is set to value 'true', the following shall be set according to the type of sharing.
FSMr3:
1. LTE-3G RF sharing. There shall be 1 SMOD instance and 1 SMOD_EXT instance with SMOD_EXT-utranSupport set to true.
2. LTE-2G RF sharing. There shall be 1 SMOD instance and 1 SMOD_EXT instance with SMOD_EXT-geranSupport set to true.
3. LTE-LTE RF sharing. There shall be 1 SMOD instance and 1 SMOD_EXT instance with SMOD_EXT-eutraSupport set to true.
4. LTE-2G + LTE-2G RF sharing. There shall be 1 SMOD instance, 1 SMOD_EXT instance with SMOD_EXT-eutraSupport set to true, and optionally 1 SMOD_EXT instance with SMOD_EXT-geranSupport set to true.
AirScale:
1. LTE-3G RF sharing. There shall be 1 SMOD instance and 1 or more SMOD_EXT instances with SMOD_EXT-utranSupport set to true.
2. LTEFDD-LTETDD RF sharing. The shared module shall be ASIRMOD and one of the following is true:
2.1. If supportedCellTechnology contains FDD then there shall be SMOD_EXT instance with SMOD_EXT-eutraTDDSupport set to true
2.2. If supportedCellTechnology contains TDD then there shall be SMOD_EXT instance with SMOD_EXT-eutraSupport set to true

If rfSharingEnabled is set to true, there cannot be any instance of RMOD-cpriARfSharing set to SECONDARY.

If rfSharingEnabled is set to true and the radio is shared, there must be two CABLINKs created:
1) One endpointDN set as the shared radio DN, another endpointDN set to an SMOD or BBMOD that is connected to the shared radio.
2) One endpointDN set as the shared radio DN, antoher endpointDN set to an SMOD_EXT that is sharing radio.

If rfSharingEnabled is set to true and the ASIRMOD is shared, there must be two CABLINKs created:
1) One endpointDN set as the shared ASIRMOD DN, another endpointDN set to a BBMOD that is connected to the shared ASIRMOD
2) One endpointDN set as the shared ASIRMOD DN, antoher endpointDN set to an SMOD_EXT that is sharing ASIRMOD

[PR207759 LTE-GSM RF sharing]
If rfSharingEnabled is set to true and SMOD_EXT-geranSupport is set to true, the following NOTE instances must be configured:
   For the SMOD_EXT with geranSupport set to true, there is a NOTE-attribute set to attribute.attribName="2G_SMOD", attribute.attrValue=<within the range of 1..3 and does not overlap with LTE SMOD-sModId>, describedObjDN=<DN of corresponding SMOD_EXT>
   For each shared RMOD, there is one and only one NOTE-attribute set to attribute.attribName="2G_RMOD", attribute.attrValue=<within the range of 1..36 and unique amongst NOTEs with attribName=2G_RMOD>, describedObjDN=<DN of corresponding RMOD>
   For each shared ANTL, there is one and only one NOTE-attribute set to attribute.attribName="2G_ANTL", attribute.attrValue=<within the range of 1..216 and unique amongst NOTEs with attribName=2G_ANTL>, describedObjDN=<DN of corresponding ANTL>
   For each shared LNA, there is one and only one NOTE-attribute set to attribute.attribName="2G_MHA", attribute.attrValue=<within the range of 1..255 and unique amongst NOTEs with attribName=2G_MHA>, describedObjDN=<DN of corresponding LNA>
   For each shared RET, there is one and only one NOTE-attribute set to attribute.attribName="2G_RET", attribute.attrValue=<within the range of 1..255 and unique amongst NOTEs with attribName=2G_RET>, describedObjDN=<DN of corresponding RET>

   If there are no shared radios between LTE and GSM, the above NOTE instances must not be configured.

   Parameter describedObjDN  cannot be referencing a no-shared object. i.e. dedicated radio module, ANTL connected to dedicated radio module, MHA/RET detected from dedicated radio module when attribute.attribName gets value  "2G_SMOD"/ "2G_RMOD"/"2G_ANTL"/"2G_MHA"/"2G_RET”.
[END PR207759 LTE-GSM RF sharing]

rootSeqIndex.description: The premable generation is started from the Root Sequence which is pointed by the logical root sequence number. 64 preambles can be transmitted in the PRACH frame. If one root is not enough to generate all the 64 preambles, then the consecutive number is selected until the full set is generated. RACH root sequence is cell specific information and neighbouring cells should have a different value. RACH root sequence is transmitted in system information.
rootSeqIndex.notes:
Related functions: PRACH / RACH configuration Related parameters: LNCEL_FDD - prachCS
LNCEL_FDD - prachHsFlag The allowed range for rootSeqIndex when prachHsFlag is set to 'true' depends on the configured prachCS (PRACH cyclic shift) as below
- for prachCS set to '0' the allowed rootseqIndex values are 24..816
- for prachCS set to '1' the allowed rootseqIndex values are 30..810
- for prachCS set to '2' the allowed rootseqIndex values are 36..804
- for prachCS set to '3' the allowed rootseqIndex values are 42..796
- for prachCS set to '4' the allowed rootseqIndex values are 52..787
- for prachCS set to '5' the allowed rootseqIndex values are 64..779
- for prachCS set to '6' the allowed rootseqIndex values are 76..764 
- for prachCS set to '7' the allowed rootseqIndex values are 90..749
- for prachCS set to '8' the allowed rootseqIndex values are 116..732
- for prachCS set to '9' the allowed rootseqIndex values are 136..704
- for prachCS set to '10' the allowed rootseqIndex values are 168..676
- for prachCS set to '11' the allowed rootseqIndex values are 204..616
- for prachCS set to '12' the allowed rootseqIndex values are 264..566
- for prachCS set to '13' the allowed rootseqIndex values are 328..498
- for prachCS set to '14' the allowed rootseqIndex values are 384..450

IPRTV6 - ipRtV6Id

routingTablePtr.description:
A reference to a routing table. This is a distinguished name referencing an instance of class IPRT or IPRTV6.
Format: "FTM-1/IPNO-1/IPRT-1" or  "FTM-1/IPNO-1/IPRTV6-1"

where
FTM-1: = a parent instance of object class IPNO, This is always 1 (static MO)
IPNO-1: = a parent instance of object class IPRT, 
IPRT-#: # = an instance of object class IPRT
IPRTV6-#: # = an instance of object class IPRTV6

A policy may refer also to the main routing table.

Example: FTM-1/IPNO-1/IPRT-1

Note: FSMr2 supports only IPRT-1.

1000000 microseconds (Default value is 1 000 000 microseconds (1 second).
The value  1 000 000 microseconds means that the alarm will never be raised.)
rttAlarmThreshold.description:
This parameter defines the threshold, in microseconds, for raising the TWAMP session alarm for reasons of excessive round-trip-time (RTT).
The alarm is raised if the average round-trip-time of the TWAMP messages, calculated during a 1-minute evaluation period, equals or exceeds the configured threshold. The alarm will be cleared if, during 5 consecutive 1-minute periods, the average value of the RTT remains below the threshold.
Setting the value of this parameter to 1 000 000 microseconds means that the alarm will never be raised.

- at least one instance of REDRT with redirRAT 'cdma20001xRTT' must be created with configured emerCallPrio

rttStrengthThresh.description:
Defines the pilot  strength threshold  for enhanced CSFB to CDMA2000 1xRTT.
In 3GPP TS36.331, pilotStrength's range is [0 .. 63] which is different from current value range of paramter "rttStrengthThresh". The reason is that : in future phase 2 e1xCsfb feature, this parameter may be re-used as AggregatedThreshold which include strengths from multiple PNs and AggregatedThreshold 's value range is [-18 .. 63]. 

The formula used by the UE to report the pilot strength is [ -2 * 10 * log (measured pilot strength) ].
Therefore 63 maps to -31.5 dB. So [-18..63] maps to [9..-31.5] dB.
rttStrengthThresh.notes: Related functions: Handover Control (Inter RAT CDMA2000)

s1PrdRevalWaitTmr.description:
If for an inter-eNB LTE Neighbour Relation (NR) without available X2 link a handover preparation is started and since the last validation of the NR at least  the time 's1PrdRevalWaitTmr' has elapsed, then eNB triggers a re-validation for this NR via CGI measurement (if CGI measurements are allowed).

If 's1PrdRevalWaitTmr' is set to '0', then no re-validation is triggered.
Note 1: To limit the load due to re-validations, eNB triggers  re-validation only if at least some minimum wait time since last validation of the same NR has expired.
Note 2: To retrieve the CGI measurement for the re-validation, the eNB will start Active ANR mode and use a UE different from the one which needs the handover.

sCellActivationMethod.description:
This parameter defines the method to be used for SCell activation.
The meaning of the values is as follows:
'blind' means that SCell is blindly activated and it is never re-activated after the expiration of the timer sCellDeactivationTimerEnb.
'nonGBRBufferBased' means that SCell activation is triggered depending on the non-GBR data in the buffer. For a UE with two configured SCells, SCell activation is triggered depending on the non-GBR data in the buffer in a joint way, i.e., one MAC CE command activates all SCells.
'nonGBRBufferBasedStepWise' means that for a UE with two configured SCells, SCell activation by one or more separate MAC CE command(s) is triggered depending on the non-GBR data in buffer in a step-wise way. In the first step one SCell is activated depending on the non-GBR data in buffer and after that depending on the non-GBR data in buffer the second SCell is activated if needed.

Note: The period of the SCell activation cycle is configured in sCellActivationCyclePeriod.

With actULCAggr=UL_CA_with_smartSched, a DL&UL sCell's activation will be triggered by eNB to reach fast load balance purpose, this kind of sCell activation trigger scheme works without regard to sCellActivationMethod setting.

sCellDeactivationTimereNB.description:
This timer controls the deactivation of Secondary Cell for Carrier Aggregation configured UEs.

The timer behaves in the same way as the SCell deactivation timer defined in TS 36.321, but result is explicit SCell deactivation by MAC CE instead of implicit SCell deactivation in order to avoid eNB – UE misalignment due to ambiguous HARQ feedback.
The value represents the number of radio frames.
Value "infinity" means that the SCell is never deactivated by sCellDeactivationTimereNB.

sCellpCellHARQFdbkUsage.description:
The parameter selects how the ambiguous HARQ feedback of UE with an active SCell related to DL transmission shall be interpreted for the purpose of controlling 
1) DRX Inactivity Timer, and 
2) radio link problem detection/recovery in PCell.

If set to conservative, the ambiguous HARQ feedback is interpreted as DTX for the purpose of controlling the timer and as DTX for radio link problem detection, the ambiguous HARQ feedback is ignored for radio link problem recovery. 
If set to aggressive, the ambiguous HARQ feedback is interpreted as NACK for the purpose of controlling the timer and as NACK for radio link problem recovery, the ambiguous HARQ feedback is ignored for radio link problem detection. It is expected that the aggressive setting will favor the UE throughput of UEs with an active SCell.
It is expected that the conservative setting will favor cell throughput.
sCellpCellHARQFdbkUsage.fullName: SCell and PCell ambiguous HARQ feedback usage

sFreqPrioDfs.description:
sFreqPrioDfs enters into the comparison between candidate SCells. This comparison is based on a measure of the average load, and can be biased towards a cell by giving it (or its frequency layer) a higher priority. 

Use sFreqPrioDfs = 1 (default) for highest priority, sFreqPrioDfs = 10000 for lowest priority.

Note2: sFreqPrioDfs is used in connection with unlicensed SCells within th UNII-2 band, whereas sFreqPrio is used in connection with SCells from either licensed bands or UNII-1/3 bands.

This parameter specifies the IP address to be used for synchronization plane traffic. The IP address has to collapse with a network interface IP address. The synchronization plane IP address may collapse with the uPlaneIpAddress, the mPlaneIpAddress and the cPlaneIpAddress.
This parameter supports both IPv4 and IPv6 addresses. 

For IPv4, the parameter has to be entered in dotted decimal format.
For IPv6, the parameter has to be entered according to formats specified in RFC2460. 
Note 1: " ToP feature (TOPF) is not supported for TDD release and only 0.0.0.0 address can be configured to S-plane IP address"
Note 2: Validation doesnot prevent from configuring virtual IP addresses.

TOPP - actTopPhaseSynch: If actTopPhaseSynch is 'true', sPlaneIpAddress has to be configured in case IP unicast mode is used.

scellActivationLevel.description:
The parameter configures aggressiveness/conservativeness level of SCell activation. The higher the value of the parameter the more conservative the SCell activation is.
If configured to value X, the meaning is as follows:
if it is estimated that the current UE data in the buffer is more than what can be drained on the PCell/PCell+ currently active SCell during the next X TTIs, then one SCell/one additional SCell will be activated (when sCellActivationMethod is configured to the value 'nonGBRBufferBased' and one SCell is configured for a UE or when sCellActivationMethod is configured to the value 'nonGBRBufferBasedStepWise' and one or two SCells are configured for a UE).
if it is estimated that the current UE data in the buffer is more than what can be drained on the PCell during the next X TTIs, then two SCells will be activated (when sCellActivationMethod is configured to the value 'nonGBRBufferBased' and two SCells are configured for a UE).

Note: This parameter has no effect if sCellActivationMethod is configured to 'blind'.

scellBadChQualThr.description:
Defines the maximum modulation and coding scheme (MCS) index estimated for transmission from the secondary cell (SCell) to infer that the SCell is detected with bad channel quality by the served UE. If the estimated MCS index is smaller than this threshold for the pre-defined decision period  (shortPeriodScellChEst  or longPeriodScellChEst ), data transmission from the SCell is suspended and, depending on the configured multScellReleaseTimer parameter value,  multScellReleaseTimer is started. 
The "MCS" mentioned here is the "wideband MCS", i.e. it is assumed that all the PRBs are used for transmission.
scellBadChQualThr.fullName: Threshold for a SCell detected -  bad channel quality

schedulType.description:
This parameter specifies how the EPS bearer with QCI 5 is scheduled.
For the scheduling type “SIGNALLING” the bearer is handled like SRBs. The MAC LCGID shall be set to 0 and schedulPrio is used for UL and DL scheduling.
For the scheduling type “NON-GBR” the bearer is handled like other non-GBR bearers. The MAC LCGID shall not be to 0 and the schedulWeight is used for DL scheduling.
schedulType.notes:
Related functions: Bearer Management (QCI Profile) Related parameters: LNBTS - lcgid
LNBTS - qciTab5-schedulPrio
LNBTS - supportedCellTechnology
LNBTS_FDD - actConvVoice
LNBTS_TDD - actConvVoice
LNBTS_TDD - actVoLteCallSteering (1) If supportedCellTechnology is configured to 'FDD' or 'TDD' or 'mixed_FDD_TDD' following conditions must be fulfilled:
(1.1) If qciTab5-schedulType is set to 'NON-GBR', schedulPrio must be equal or greater than '9'.

(2) If the supportedCellTechnology is configured to 'FDD' following conditions must be fulfilled in addition to (1):
(2.1) If actConvVoice in LNBTS_FDD is set to 'false', qciTab5-schedulType must be set to 'NON-GBR'.

(3) If the supportedCellTechnology is configured to 'TDD' following conditions must be fulfilled in addition to (1):
(3.1) If (actConvVoice in LNBTS_TDD is set to 'false') AND (actVoLteCallSteering in LNBTS_TDD is set to 'false'), qciTab5-schedulType must be set to 'NON-GBR'.

(4) If the supportedCellTechnology is configured to 'mixed_FDD_TDD' conditions of (2) AND (3) must be fulfilled in addition to (1).

sctpWaitTimeInitSeqRetry.description:
This parameter defines the wait time the eNB waits until it tries to re-initialize the SCTP association (S1 and X2 OAM controlled)
Case A: after having tried unsucessfully to establish an association to a peer with a SCTP sequence  
Case B: After reception of SCTP SHUTDOWN/ABORT
The value defines a fixed time period. In addition, eNB adds an equally distributed random time period between 0 and 60s to the configured value.

This prevents the eNBs to which the network element that has sent the SCTP shutdown command (e.g. MME) will be overflooded by SCTP intialization from multiple eNBs.
sctpWaitTimeInitSeqRetry.fullName: Wait Time before starting SCTP init after shutdown
sctpWaitTimeInitSeqRetry.source: Nokia LTE18 official BTS parameter dictionary (FDD)

sdlPrimaryDestIp.description:
Indicates the IP address or Fully Qualified Domain Name (FQDN) of the primary destination for Session Detail Log (SDL) data.

For IPv4, the parameter has to be entered in dotted decimal format.

For IPv6, the parameter has to be entered according to formats specified in RFC2460.

IPv4 address ranges:
It is not allowed to configure the address 0.0.0.0, the broadcast address 255.255.255.255 or an address within the range of multicast addresses
(224.0.0.0-239.255.255.255) or loop-back addresses (127.0.0.0-127.255.255.255).

IPv6 address ranges:
It is recommended to configure only an address within the range of Unique Local Unicast addresses (FC00::/7) or Global Unicast addresses (2000::/3).

searchAllCandForEmergency.description:
Determines if special preemption rules shall be applied for emergency sessions.

Yes: 
In case of an emergency session, candidates are searched in other PLMNs  if no candidates are found in the list of preferred preemption candidates (preferredPreempCandList).
'Other PLMNs' means either PLMNs of the cell or of cells in the same baseband pool with the same preemption profile assigned which are not in the list of preferred preemption candidates.

applyRulesForRegularUsers :
The same preemption rules are applied as for regular users.
searchAllCandForEmergency.fullName: Seach all candidates in case of emergency sessions
searchAllCandForEmergency.notes:
Related functions: Radio Admission Control Related parameters: LNBTS - act1xCsfb
LNBTS - actCsfbPsHoToUtra
LNBTS - actDualRx1xCsfb
LNBTS - actEmerCallRedir
LNBTS - actPlmnBasedPreemption
LNBTS_FDD - actIMSEmerSessR9
LNBTS_TDD - actIMSEmerSessR9
LNCEL - cellTechnology If searchAllCandForEmergency is set to 'yes' it must be ensured that emergency call handling is activated in the eNB. This means that depending on the cellTechnology of LNCEL instances referencing the profile at least one of the following parameters must be set to 'true'. The following checks are not relevant if the profile is not yet referenced by any LNCEL instance.

If actPlmnBasedPreemption is set to 'true' and if cellTechnology of all LNCEL instances referring to the PREEMPPR instance is 'FDD' then at least one of the following parameters must be set to 'true': act1xCsfb, actDualRx1xCsfb, actCsfbPsHoToUtra, actEmerCallRedir or LNBTS_FDD-actIMSEmerSessR9.

If actPlmnBasedPreemption is set to 'true' and if cellTechnology of all LNCEL instances referring to the PREEMPPR instance is 'TDD' then at least one of the following parameters must be set to 'true': act1xCsfb, actDualRx1xCsfb, actCsfbPsHoToUtra, actEmerCallRedir or LNBTS_TDD-actIMSEmerSessR9.

Otherwise at least one of the following parameters must be set to 'true if actPlmnBasedPreemption is set to 'true' :
act1xCsfb, actDualRx1xCsfb, actCsfbPsHoToUtra, actEmerCallRedir or (LNBTS_FDD-actIMSEmerSessR9  and LNBTS_TDD-actIMSEmerSessR9).

selectOuterPuschRegion.description:
This parameter activates the feature LTE825 'Uplink outer region scheduling' by selecting the target UL outer scheduling region for PUSCH and PRACH. When the feature is activated, additional PRBs in the outer region of the UL spectrum are allocated for PUSCH and PRACH scheduling.
The feature LTE825 'Uplink outer region scheduling' is deactivated if parameter is set to 'None'.
The outer region is conform to the blanked PUCCH PRBs.
selectOuterPuschRegion.notes:
Related functions: Scheduler (Miscellaneous) Related parameters: APUCCH_FDD - selectPrachRegion
LNCEL - nCqiRb
LNCEL_FDD - actAutoPucchAlloc
LNCEL_FDD - actCatM
LNCEL_FDD - actUlPwrRestrScn
LNCEL_FDD - blankedPucch
LNCEL_FDD - prachFreqOff
LNCEL_FDD - ulChBw (1.1) selectOuterPuschRegion can only be set to 'UpperEdge' or 'LowerEdge' if ulChBw is equal to or greater than 5 MHz.
(1.2) If actUlPwrRestrScn is not set to 'none' then selectOuterPuschRegion must be set to 'None'.
(1.3) if actCatM is set to 'true', then selectOuterPuschRegion must be set to 'none'. 

(2) For ulChBw of '5 MHz', '10 MHz', '15 MHz' and '20 MHz':
(2.1) if selectOuterPuschRegion is configured to 'None' or blankedPucch is less than '12', then the allowed prachFreqOff range is:
- roundup ((MaxPucchResourceSize + blankedPucch) / 2) … ulChBw (in PRBs) - 6 - roundup ((MaxPucchResourceSize + blankedPucch) / 2)
(2.2) if selectOuterPuschRegion is configured to 'LowerEdge' and blankedPucch is greater than or equal to '12', then the allowed prachFreqOff ranges are:
- (0 ... roundup (blankedPucch/2) - 6) and 
- (roundup ((MaxPucchResourceSize + blankedPucch) / 2) … ulChBw (in PRBs) - 6 - roundup ((MaxPucchResourceSize + blankedPucch) / 2))
(2.3) if selectOuterPuschRegion is configured to 'UpperEdge' and blankedPucch is greater than or equal to '12', then the allowed prachFreqOff ranges are:
- (roundup ((MaxPucchResourceSize + blankedPucch) / 2) … ulChBw (in PRBs) - 6 - roundup ((MaxPucchResourceSize + blankedPucch) / 2)) and 
- ((ulChBw(in PRBs) – roundup (blankedPuccch/2)) ... ulChBw(in PRBs) – 6)

Note: MaxPucchResourceSize is calculated in nCqiRb.

The following conditions in (3.x) are applicable in APUCCH_FDD of the cell only if actAutoPucchAlloc is set to 'true':
(3.1) If selectOuterPuschRegion is set to 'UpperEdge', selectPrachRegion in APUCCH_FDD of the same LNCEL_FDD can NOT be configured to 'OuterLowerEdge'.
(3.2) If selectOuterPuschRegion is set to 'LowerEdge', selectPrachRegion in APUCCH_FDD of the same LNCEL_FDD can NOT be configured to 'OuterUpperEdge'.

selectPrachRegion.description: Using this parameter, the operator defines the selected PRACH region. If LTE1130 'Dynamic PUCCH allocation' is activated, the system automatically selects the PRACH PRB offset in this region.
selectPrachRegion.fullName: Selection of PRACH region in automatic PUCCH allocation
selectPrachRegion.notes:
Related functions: PHY/MAC Configuration (Uplink) Related parameters: APUCCH_FDD - blankedPucch
CHANNEL - resourceDN
LNCEL_FDD - actAutoPucchAlloc
LNCEL_FDD - actCatM
LNCEL_FDD - actMMimo
LNCEL_FDD - actUlPwrRestrScn
LNCEL_FDD - dlChBw
LNCEL_FDD - earfcnDL
LNCEL_FDD - earfcnUL
LNCEL_FDD - prachConfIndex
LNCEL_FDD - selectOuterPuschRegion All of the following conditions are only applicable if actAutoPucchAlloc is set to 'true'.
If selectOuterPuschRegion is set to 'UpperEdge', selectPrachRegion can NOT be configured to 'OuterLowerEdge'.
If selectOuterPuschRegion is set to 'LowerEdge', selectPrachRegion can NOT be configured to 'OuterUpperEdge'.
Only if selectPrachRegion is set to 'OuterUpperEdge', actUlPwrRestrScn can be configured to 'band18_26'.
Only if selectPrachRegion is set to 'InnerUpperEdge', actUlPwrRestrScn can be configured to ('band30_NS21' or 'band13_NS07' or 'band1_NS05').
Only if selectPrachRegion is set to 'InnerLowerEdge', actCatM can be set to 'true'.

For any two cells in the eNB, if (actMMimo is 'true') AND (resourceDN is the same) AND (earfcnDL is the same) AND (earfcnUL is the same), the two cell shall be called as dual-cell (two cells on the same carrier), all of the following conditions must be fulfilled:
- prachConfIndex must have the same value in both cells
- dlChBw must have the same value in both cells
- selectPrachRegion parameter must have the same value in both cells
- blankedPucch parameter must have the same value in both cells

shapingOverhead.description:
This parameter defines whether the shaper accounts for the Ethernet frame or IP packet data for scheduling and shaping calculations, and ignores the corresponding overhead.

Ethernet frame:
Considers Ethernet protocol fields from destination MAC address to the frame check sequence (FCS) (including possible Ethernet padding), thus ignoring the overhead of Ethernet IPG, Preamble and SFD field.

IP packet:
Considers all IP protocol fields, thus ignoring the overhead of Ethernet encapsulation.

EUTRA-EUTRA – 1 or more radio modules are shared between LTE and another LTE

siRepPatternCatM.description:
The parameter SI Repetition Pattern defines the common System Information scheduling repetition pattern for all SIs of Cat-M UEs.
This is broadcasted in SIB1-BR.
Refer to 3GPP 36.331 and IE si-RepetitionPattern-r13.
Note: All Cat-M UEs in RRC Connected mode will be released when this parameter is online modified.
siRepPatternCatM.notes:
Related functions: System Information Broadcast (Control) Related parameters: CATMCEL - actDlPciBasedNarBandCatM
CATMCEL - numCELevelCatM
CATMCEL - siNarBandSelectionCatM
CATMPR - sib16PeriodicityCatM
CATMPR - sib2PeriodicityCatM
CATMPR - sib3sib4PeriodicityCatM
CATMPR - sib5PeriodicityCatM
LNBTS - actUTCBroadcast
SIB - sibSchedulingList 1) If numCELevelCatM is set to '1' or '2', siRepPatternCatM only can be set to 'every4thRF' or 'every8thRF'.
2) If siRepPatternCatM is set to 'every2ndRF', the following conditions must be fulfilled:
  - actDlPciBasedNarBandCatM must be set to ‘true’.
  - siNarBandSelectionCatM must be set to ‘ModeB’.

3) The following condition must be fulfilled:  si_overhead <= 32%.
'si_overhead' represents the percent of radio frame used for CatM SI messages, and is calculated as below from step1 to step3.
siRepPatternCatM value mapping for the following formula {every2ndRF:20, every4thRF: 40, every8thRF: 80}
step1: si_overhead = ceil(siWindowLenCatM/siRepPatternCatM)*10/sib2PeriodicityCatM;
step2: If sibType5 is configured in sibSchedulingList and at least one CATMIRFIM instance is configured, 
                 si_overhead += ceil(siWindowLenCatM/siRepPatternCatM)*10/sib3sib4PeriodicityCatM,
                 si_overhead += ceil(siWindowLenCatM/siRepPatternCatM)*10/sib5PeriodicityCatM,
             else if sibType4 is configured in sibSchedulingList.
                 si_overhead += ceil(siWindowLenCatM/siRepPatternCatM)*10/sib3sib4PeriodicityCatM;
step3: If sibType16 is configured in sibSchedulingList and actUTCBroadcast is set to 'true', si_overhead += ceil(siWindowLenCatM/siRepPatternCatM)*10/sib16PeriodicityCatM.

- actCMAS is set to 'true'
- sib2xTransmit is set to 'true'.

Conditions in (2.x) are valid in addition to (1.x) if the cellTechnology of the parent LNCEL instance is configured to 'FDD':
(2.1) siWindowLen value 1ms shall not be used when there are more than 5 SIBs set in siMessageSibType (i.e. sib2Scheduling, sib3Scheduling and three in sibSchedulingList)
(2.2) If (actOtdoa is set to 'true') AND (prsConfigurationIndex >= 151) , following condition must be fulfilled:
- (max. siWindowLen) less than or equal ((min ((smallest si[x]Periodicity), (PRS period)) – 10 ms) / (# of SIBs (sets in structure sibSchedulingList +2)),
where depending on the prsConfigurationIndex PRS period in above equation is set to 
PRS period =
- 160 ms for prsConfigurationIndex = {151, 152, 153, 156, 157}
- 320 ms for prsConfigurationIndex = {471, 472, 473, 476, 477}
- 640 ms for prsConfigurationIndex = {1111, 1112, 1113, 1116, 1117}
- 1280 ms for prsConfigurationIndex = {2391, 2392, 2393, 2396, 2397}
where si[x]Periodicity is the smallest periodicity value in all defined siMessagePeriodicity.
(2.3) If dlChBw is set to '1.4 MHz' or '3 MHz', siWindowLen must be greater than or equal to '10ms'.
(2.4) In addition to (1.2) siWindowLen must be greater than or equal to '20ms' if one of the following conditions is fulfilled:
- actEicic is set to 'true'
- actLiquidCell is set to 'true'.
(2.5) If (actCMAS or actETWS or sib2xTransmit is set to 'true') AND actOtdoa is set to 'true' AND prsConfigurationIndex is > 150 AND siWindowLen is set to '20 ms' AND the number of configured SIBs (i.e. the number of sets in structure sibSchedulingList + 2) is 8 or higher, then LNCEL_FDD-prsConfigurationIndex must be set to one of the following values: '471', '1111' or '2391'. 
(2.6) If (actCMAS or actETWS or sib2xTransmit is set to 'true') AND actOtdoa is set to 'true' AND prsConfigurationIndex is > 150 AND siWindowLen is set to '40 ms' AND the number of configured SIBs (i.e. the number of sets in structure sibSchedulingList + 2) is 8 or higher, then LNCEL_FDD-prsConfigurationIndex must be set to one of the following values: '1111' or '2391'.
(2.7) If actMBMS is equal to 'true' then ... 
- siWindowLen must be greater than or equal to '5ms' in all SIB instances belonging to LNCEL instances with earfcnDL in LNCEL_FDD of this cell equal to mbsfnEarfcn in MBSFNSYNCAREA_FDD and dlChBw in same LNCEL_FDD of this cell equal to mbsfnDlChBw in same MBSFNSYNCAREA_FDD
- siWindowLen must be set to the same value in all SIB instances belonging to LNCEL instances with earfcnDL in LNCEL_FDD of this cell equal to mbsfnEarfcn in MBSFNSYNCAREA_FDD and dlChBw in same LNCEL_FDD of this cell equal to mbsfnDlChBw in same MBSFNSYNCAREA_FDD.
(2.8) actMicroDtx can only be set to 'true' if siWindowLen is set to '10ms', '20ms' or '40ms'.

(2.9) If (dlMimoMode is set to ('Closed Loop MIMO (4x2)' OR 'Closed Loop MIMO (4x4)' OR 'Closed Loop MIMO (8x2)' OR 'Closed Loop MIMO (8x4)') AND (activatedMimoTM is NOT set to 'TM4') ,
(2.9.1) if actEicic is set to 'true', siWindowLen must be configured = '40ms'
(2.9.2) if actEicic is set to 'false', siWindowLen must be configured >= '20ms'

(2.10) If prsConfigurationIndex is set to any of the allowed values <151 then no restrictions on siWindowLen apply based on this parameter.
(2.11) If actCatM is set to 'true'
(2.11.1) If actEicic is set to 'false', siWindowLen must have a value greater than or equal to '20ms'.
(2.11.2) If actEicic is set to 'true', siWindowLen must be equal to '40ms'.
(2.12) if actDlSlimCarrier is set to true and numBlankDlPrbsUp+ numBlankDlPrbsDown >0 
(2.12.1) If dlChBw is set to '5 MHz', siWindowLen must be greater than or equal to '10ms'.

Conditions in (3.x) are valid in addition to (1.x) if the cellTechnology of the parent LNCEL instance is configured to 'TDD':
(3.1) siWindowLen must be configured to '5ms' or higher values
(3.2) If actOtdoa is set to 'true', following condition must be fulfilled:
- (max. siWindowLen) less than or equal ((min ((smallest si[x]Periodicity), (PRS period)) – 10 ms) / (# of SIBs (sets in structure sibSchedulingList +2)),
where depending on the prsConfigurationIndex PRS period in above equation is set to 
PRS period =
- 160 ms for prsConfigurationIndex = 153 … 159
- 320 ms for prsConfigurationIndex = 473… 479
- 640 ms for prsConfigurationIndex = 1113 … 1119
- 1280 ms for prsConfigurationIndex = 2393 … 2399
where si[x]Periodicity is the smallest periodicity value in all defined siMessagePeriodicity.
(3.3a) TDD Flexi Zone Micro: If eICIC is activated in non-macro (medium, small, verysmall) cells, i.e. cellType is set to 'medium', 'small' or 'verysmall' AND actEicic has value 'true', following condition must be fulfilled:
- if siMessageRepetition in any of the sib2Scheduling, sib3Scheduling or sibSchedulingList is greater than '2', siWindowLen must be set to '40 ms', else siWindowLen must be set to a value greater than or equal to '20 ms'
(3.3b) TDD Macro eNB: If eICIC is activated in macro cells, i.e., cellType is set to 'large' AND actEicic has value 'true', following condition must be fulfilled:
